title: Mexico Reinforces Search Strategy with 10 Actions; Reports 13,625 People Located
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [September 4, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/gobierno-refuerza-
estrategia-de-busqueda-con-10-acciones-reporta-13-mil-625-localizaciones/),
one of Mexico’s leading investigative magazines._

The government of Mexico reinforced the National Strategy for the Search and
Location of Missing or Disappeared Persons with ten actions aimed at improving
the records of disappeared persons, ensuring that every report has an
investigation file, speeding up searches, strengthening forensic
identification, and expanding the operational capacity of the National Search
Commission, in addition to bringing attention directly to families and to the
states.

Of the **31,946 people located** that President **Claudia Sheinbaum** reported
on March 27, 2026, **13,625** correspond to **locations obtained since July
2025** through the mechanisms that form part of the search and location
strategy now being reinforced.

The figure, presented during the presidential morning press conference by
Arturo Medina Padilla, undersecretary of Human Rights, Population, and
Migration, comprises the results of the **Single Identity Platform** ,
coordination with the states, the **National Immediate Search Alert** , and
searches carried out directly in the field.

According to the breakdown given by the official, **6,939 people were
located** through the **Single Identity Platform** ; **3,039** through
**coordinated work with the states** ; **2,572** through the **National
Immediate Search Alert** ; and **1,075** as a result of **searches in the
field**.

The **31,946 people located** were reported by Sheinbaum during her morning
press conference on **March 27, 2026** , as the cumulative result from the
start of her administration, in October 2024, up to that cutoff.

In contrast, the **13,625** were presented **this past September 3** as
locations obtained through the search mechanisms implemented or strengthened
since July 2025.

It is on that search structure that the ten actions announced by the
government are organized. Medina Padilla explained at the morning press
conference of **September 3, 2026** , that “these 10 actions that the
president instructed us [to carry out] […] are organized around the **National
Strategy for the Search and Location of Missing or Disappeared Persons**.”

The first pillar proposes “**Ensuring that all reports in the National
Registry of Disappeared and Missing Persons have complete data**.” The
objective is to improve the information available from the outset, since the
quality of the data determines the possibilities of establishing a search
route.

To this end, Medina Padilla explained that, together with bodies such as the
United Nations and UN Human Rights, “a group of **national and international
experts** ” was formed “with whom a **technical, scientific review of the
registry** will be carried out in order to organize this registry and make
decisions about it.”

The review seeks to determine what to do with the records that have sufficient
information and with those that present incomplete data. The final purpose,
the official noted, is “**to be able to turn the registry into an effective
search tool**.”

The second point establishes “**Ensuring that every disappearance report has
an investigation file**.” With this, the aim is to make it possible to assign
responsibilities and activate investigation mechanisms. “That there be a
responsible authority: **the Public Prosecutor’s Office** , that there be
expert examinations, that there be a **formal search plan** , **within the
framework of an investigation file** ,” Medina Padilla explained.

The measure also seeks to allow cases in which a possible crime exists to move
toward investigation and the eventual punishment of those responsible. The
undersecretary stressed that “**not all absences or failures to locate are
disappearances, and this is very important**.”

The third point is “**Reporting on the progress in the search and location of
persons**.” It is precisely in this section that the federal government seeks
to organize the information on results and make visible which mechanisms have
made it possible to find people.

At the **September 3** press conference, Medina Padilla explained that the
locations are the result of work involving the **CNB** and other institutions,
among them authorities of **the Interior Ministry** and the **National
Population Registry (Renapo)** , through the **Single Identity Platform**. The
objective of making this progress transparent is for families to know the
status of the searches and for the results to be evaluated in a differentiated
manner.

The fourth pillar consists of “**Reporting on the progress of the National
Immediate Search Alert (ANBI)** ,” one of the central mechanisms of rapid
reaction to a disappearance.

In this regard, the president explained that the Immediate Search Response
Center makes it possible to activate the authorities from the moment the
report is received. “If there is a person who reports a missing or unlocated
family member, they immediately alert this Immediate Alert Response Center
that same day.”

She added that “most of the people who are reported are found the same day,”
while Omar García Harfuch reported in a post on his account on the social
network X that **50 percent of the people reported through the ANBI are
located within the first 24 hours**.

The fifth point consists of “**Strengthening searches in hospitals, detention
centers, and other institutions**.” The measure seeks to expand the
possibilities of finding people who may be physically located, but whose
identity could not be established or who provided a different name.

“We are going to strengthen the **search in hospitals, detention centers** ,
to locate people whose name is perhaps unknown due to **a lack of
identification or who gave a different name** ,” Medina Padilla explained, and
noted that this is one of the requests repeatedly raised by the collectives.

The sixth pillar is “**Implementing the Human Identification Plan to reduce
the forensic backlog together with the Attorney General’s Office** ,” based on
three points: carrying out a diagnosis of unidentified deceased persons who
are in safekeeping centers; strengthening those spaces to carry out the
corresponding analyses; and reducing the backlog in DNA tests.

The search, according to the government, maintains locating people alive as a
priority, but also requires developing capacities to identify deceased persons
when it is not possible to find them alive. “Here it must be said that **we
always prioritize the search for the living** ,” Medina Padilla noted.

The seventh point incorporates a preventive dimension: “**Preventing the
recruitment and co-optation of young people through digital platforms**.”
Since the start of the administration, the undersecretary reported, **more
than 1,700 account profiles** that made false invitations to young people,
mainly through supposed job offers, have been deactivated, and **more than
12,500 messages** have also been removed.

The eighth pillar establishes “**Expanding the operational, technical, and
human capacities of the National Search Commission with specialized personnel
and equipment**.”

The **Second Government Report** stated that the operational personnel of the
CNB and the National Network of Searchers reached **354 experts** ,
distributed across 26 states and specialized in **criminology, criminalistics,
geophysics, forensic sciences, archaeology, physical anthropology, dentistry,
and other disciplines**.

During the presentation of the ten actions, Medina Padilla also reported on
the hiring of specialized personnel and the incorporation of equipment such as
**drones and ground-penetrating radar** to strengthen forensic searches.

The ninth point proposes “**Maintaining ongoing attention and dialogue with
the families of disappeared persons and collectives**.” The strategy
contemplates sustaining contact with families, not only to report results, but
also to build search routes and address the particular needs of each case.

Between September 2025 and June 2026, the Second Government Report recorded
attention to **221 collectives from 29 states** , in addition to nine brigades
for taking and delivering genetic samples in which more than 550 members of
families and collectives from seven states took part.

Medina Padilla, for his part, reported that **more than 13,300 assistance
sessions and meetings** with families and collectives were held in Mexico
City, in the states, and in the field.

The tenth pillar seeks to transfer that attention scheme directly to the
states: “**Bringing the Strategy to the territory through visits to the states
in family-assistance sessions and coordination with the states**.”

The intention is for families to be able to receive regional attention and for
the strategy not to depend exclusively on meetings in Mexico City. Medina
Padilla announced a new national session to explain to the collectives the
methodology and the results achieved, and to verify that the cases have an
investigation file and that DNA samples have been taken when necessary.

## The 284 Locations in the Second Report Correspond to a Specific Cutoff

The figure of **284 people located** that appears in the Second Government
Report requires an additional clarification because it **does not represent
the total of people located during the administration, nor does it contradict
the figures of 31,946 or 13,625**.

The Second Report, which covers the period from **September 1, 2025, to June
30, 2026** , states that during those ten months **6,679 search actions** were
carried out: **3,581 search-for-the-living actions and 3,098 forensic and
criminalistic actions**. As a result of those actions, **284 locations were
reported: 198 alive and 86 dead** , an increase of 16.6 percent compared to
the previous period.

Therefore, the 284 locations correspond to the result of **that specific set
of search actions carried out during that period** , and not to the entire
universe of locations obtained through all the mechanisms of the national
strategy.

The Second Report itself documents, for example, that through **155
geolocation requests to the National Intelligence Center, 47 people were
located alive** , while, in coordination with the FGR and prosecutors’ offices
from 13 states, **1,005 search proceedings** were carried out.

For this reason, the figures must be read according to the components measured
in each universe: **31,946 people located** was the cumulative figure reported
by the president on March 27, 2026; **13,625 locations** was the cutoff
presented on September 3, 2026, for the mechanisms linked to the strategy
since July 2025; and **284 locations** is the result recorded in the Second
Report for the search actions carried out between September 2025 and June
2026.

In that context, the purpose of the ten new actions presented by the federal
government is to make the authorities’ response capacity more systematic; it
is not only about increasing field searches, but about intervening from the
first report onward by having complete information, opening an investigation
file, immediately activating the alert, checking hospitals and detention
centers, strengthening forensic identification, preventing recruitment
mechanisms, expanding the capacities of the CNB, and maintaining contact with
families.

President **Claudia Sheinbaum** insisted that this is constant work: “so, like
that, every day there is permanent work, both of communication and dialogue
with the collectives.”

That permanent character will be accompanied, she announced, by periodic
reports and new territorial tours, with the aim that the strategy can be
evaluated not only by the number of people located, but also by the speed with
which a search is activated, the quality of the available information, the
existence of a ministerial investigation, and the capacity to identify those
who could not be found alive.

Thus, the central figure of the administration is that of **31,946 people
located** , while the **13,625** make it possible to identify the volume of
locations associated with the mechanisms that the government is strengthening.
